title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s security and compliance guidance for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC practices, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence collection workflows, and the process for risk exceptions. It is intended for engineers, security reviewers, auditors, and product owners who implement or validate controls.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood-hosted services (Hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private deployments), the internal control plane, developer consoles, and any customer-facing tooling that processes customer data.

Owners & Contacts

- Primary owner: Security (security@redwood.ai)
- Secondary owner: Eng-Platform (platform@redwood.ai)
- Evidence coordinator: Compliance Team (compliance@redwood.ai)
- On-call for incidents: Security Pager (see runbook)

Key Sections

1) RBAC & Authentication

Summary
- All production services must use role-based access controls backed by a central identity provider (IdP). We support SSO via SAML/OIDC with Okta as the default IdP. MFA is required for all users with elevated privileges.

Principles
- Least privilege: grant the minimal set of roles required.
- Role review cadence: quarterly reviews for all high-privilege roles.
- Separation of duties: no single role should approve changes and deploy them in production.

Role & Permission Mapping (core services)

| Role | Scope | Key Permissions | Review Cadence | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| admin | Org-wide | create/delete projects, manage billing, manage roles | quarterly | Security |
| infra-operator | Production clusters | deploy, scale, SSH (jumpbox only) | monthly | Eng-Infra |
| dev | Repo & non-prod | commit, create branches, run builds | semi-annual | Eng-Developer-Experience |
| support | Customer support tooling | view billing, view non-sensitive logs, create support tickets | quarterly | Customer Success |
| auditor | Read-only across logs & configs | read audit logs, export evidence | annual | Compliance |

Authentication requirements
- SSO via Okta for employees.
- Service identities use mTLS with certs rotated every 90 days for internal services; long-lived service tokens are forbidden.
- Short-lived workload identities: use vault-issued tokens with TTL <= 1 hour for ephemeral tasks.

Provisioning & Review Process
1. Request through the access request portal (link in team wiki).
2. Manager approval required for role grants.
3. Security reviews any admin-level grants within 48 hours.
4. Automated role attestation email triggers at the cadence defined above.

2) Audit Logging

Goals
- Ensure tamper-evident capture of security-relevant events (auth successes/failures, role changes, privilege escalations, config changes, data exports).
- Centralized storage with retention and search for investigations and audits.

What to log
- Authentication events: login, logout, token issuance, MFA failures.
- Authorization events: role grants/revokes, permission denials.
- Administrative actions: deployments, config changes, secrets access, schema migrations.
- Data access events: exports, bulk downloads, cross-region transfers.
- System alerts: SLO breaches, escalations, service restarts.

Retention & Integrity
- Audit log retention (minimum): 3 years for audit/attestation needs.
- Short-term hot-search retention: 90 days in the high-performance index (for triage).
- Cold storage: remaining period archived to immutable storage with WORM where possible.
- Integrity verification: daily hash verification and weekly snapshot signing by the compliance service.

Pipeline & Tools
- Centralized pipeline: logs forwarded to Splunk/Elastic (configurable per deployment).
- Access to audit logs limited to the auditor role; exports require approval and are logged.

Example: Audit log event JSON (stored as a single-line entry)

{"timestamp":"2028-05-01T12:34:56Z","service":"auth-service","event":"role_grant","actor":"alice@redwood.ai","target":"bob@customer.com","role":"support","request_id":"req-1234","region":"us-west-2"}

3) Data Residency & Retention

Residency Requirements
- Customer data must be hosted only in regions contractually agreed with the customer. Default hosting region is us-west-2 unless overridden by contract.
- For Dedicated and Private customers, residency constraints are enforced via routing policies and DNS/placement controls in orchestration.

Retention Policies (examples)
| Data Type | Minimum Retention | Purpose | Storage Class |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Audit logs | 3 years | Compliance & forensics | Immutable/archived |
| Request traces (index) | 90 days | Triage & observability | Hot index |
| Request payloads (user content) | configurable per customer (default 30 days) | Customer support & debug | Encrypted block storage |
| Embeddings/derived artifacts | customer-controlled | Model caching/optimization | Per-customer bucket |

Data deletion & customer requests
- Data Subject Requests (DSRs) must be handled through the Privacy workflow. For deletion requests, the Evidence Coordinator must verify contractual or regulatory holds before purging.
- Deletion steps: 1) Verify identity & scope; 2) Check holds; 3) Anonymize or destruct per retention config; 4) Log deletion event to audit trail.

4) Secure SDLC (Software Development Lifecycle)

Goals
- Integrate security across the lifecycle: design, build, test, release, and run.

Mandatory checkpoints
- Design review: for new services/features that handle customer data or secrets.
- Threat modeling: required for services with sensitive data stores or external integrations.
- Secrets management: no secrets in repo, secret scanning in CI, use Vault or cloud KMS.
- Static analysis: SAST scan run on every PR.
- Dependency policy: allowlist for high-risk libs; quarterly vulnerability sweep.
- Pen tests: external pentests for critical surfaces annually and after major releases.

Release controls
- Production deploys require two approvers for system-impacting changes (one developer + one infra/ops).
- Canary & progressive rollout for all feature flags that touch inference logic or data handling.
- Automated gating: CI must pass security checks (SAST, dependency checks, unit/integration tests) before merge.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures

Objectives
- Detect and contain security events quickly, preserve evidence, notify stakeholders, and restore operations with minimal data exposure.

Classification & SLAs
- Sev-1 (Active compromise or data exfiltration): respond within 10 minutes, full incident channel open within 30 minutes.
- Sev-2 (Unauthorized access attempt affecting multiple users): respond within 1 hour.
- Sev-3 (Single-user incident or minor security alert): respond within 4 hours.

Primary response steps (high-level)
1. Triage & confirm: gather initial telemetry (audit logs, traces, process listings).
2. Contain: isolate affected services, rotate secrets, block malicious IPs, and snapshot affected nodes for forensics.
3. Preserve evidence: export immutable snapshots and copy audit logs to a locked evidence bucket.
4. Communicate: open incident channel, notify execs and legal if data exposure suspected.
5. Remediate: apply fixes, roll back if necessary, and validate with tests.
6. Post-incident review: produce a postmortem with root cause, mitigations, and action items.

Forensics checklist
- Collect timestamps, request IDs, user IDs, console session recordings, process dumps, and network captures.
- Ensure chain-of-custody recorded in evidence ticketing system.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose
- Standardize how evidence for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, customer audits) is collected, stored, and shared.

Evidence types & owners
- Policy docs (Control owner) — Security Team.
- Configurations & architecture diagrams — Eng-Platform.
- Role attestation logs — HR & Security.
- Audit logs & integrity proofs — Compliance & Security.

Evidence collection process (numbered steps)
1. Trigger: audit request or scheduled attestation.
2. Evidence coordinator (compliance@redwood.ai) creates an evidence ticket with scope.
3. Owners collect artifacts and upload to the evidence vault (immutable bucket) with metadata.
4. Security validates artifacts and signs off; any missing items generate remediation tasks.
5. Auditor access: read-only links issued; all access is logged.

Template: Evidence metadata (single-line JSON stored with artifact)
{"artifact_id":"evid-2028-0001","type":"audit_log_snapshot","owner":"security@redwood.ai","collected_at":"2028-05-01T13:00:00Z","sha256":"<hash>","retention_until":"2031-05-01"}

7) Risk & Exceptions Process

When an organization-level control cannot be met for technical, business, or customer reasons, follow the risk exception workflow.

Exception workflow
1. Submit exception request via the risk portal with justification, compensating controls, and expiration date.
2. Security reviews within 5 business days and assigns risk rating (low/medium/high).
3. For high-risk exceptions, present to the Risk Committee. Temporary mitigations must be in place before approval.
4. Approved exceptions are time-boxed (maximum 90 days) and require a remediation plan.
4. Attestation: exception status included in quarterly security report.

Example exception: Allowing a long-lived token for a legacy integration with strict compensating logging and IP allowlisting; remediation: integration migration plan in 60 days.

Appendices

A. Template: Role Review Checklist
- List current members per role
- Verify active employment or contractor status
- Confirm need for elevated access
- Document revocations and justification

B. Retention Configuration Snippet (example)

# Example retention policy YAML for audit pipeline
retention_policy:
  hot_days: 90
  cold_archive_days: 1095
  integrity_check: daily
  wORM: true

C. Links & References
- Access request portal: /internal/access-requests
- Evidence vault docs: /internal/compliance/evidence-vault

D. Glossary
- DSR: Data Subject Request
- WORM: Write-Once-Read-Many (immutable storage)
- TTL: Time-To-Live

Notes
- This document is the canonical guidance for security and compliance controls at Redwood Inference. For customer-specific contractual obligations that differ from these defaults, follow the customer contract and open a risk exception if needed.
